rooms.105700: The wide road ends at this rutted turning-place, where cart wheels have worn deep grooves into the pale gravel. A leaning milestone, its carving too weathered to read, stands at the verge. Foothills roll away to the north and south in folds of dry grass, and the road runs on west toward the dark bulk of Castle Varok. A cold wind combs the grass without ever quite dying down.
rooms.105763: Tussocks of rust-coloured grass cover this knoll, which slopes down south to the wide road. A tangle of gorse crowds a boulder streaked white by birds, and the wind whistles through the spines. Further hills ripple away in the haze, and not a tree breaks the skyline. The turf leads on west over the rise.
rooms.105762: A shallow dip in the foothills gathers the rain, and the grass is greener and ankle-high around a small black pool. The water holds the reflection of grey clouds and a few drifting leaves. Trampled trails lead off in every direction, the southern one running down to the wide road. The air smells of wet earth and distant smoke.
rooms.105767: The ground rises to a rounded crest where a single hawthorn clings to the slope, its branches all leaning away from the hills. Sheep-tracks cut through patches of heather and bracken, and the turf is cropped short. The slope falls south toward the road and west toward more rolling country. Smoke from some distant hearth smudges the horizon.
rooms.105766: Tumbled grey stones lie in the grass here, the remains of a field wall whose builders gave up long ago. Thistles have claimed the gaps, and their purple heads nod in the wind. Paths of beaten earth fork off toward the other knolls, one climbing north, another falling south. A low humming rises from bees in the heather.
rooms.105768: The foothills fold themselves around a bowl of bracken, russet and brittle at this season, that crackles as you pass. A dead oak stands on the lip of the bowl, split by lightning and bleached white as a bone. Tracks lead on north and west across the slopes, while south the ground falls away toward more heather. High above, a lone hawk hangs in the pale sky.
rooms.105776: A drystone wall, half fallen, marches along the side of this hill and then loses heart in a heap of mossy rubble. Yellow gorse flowers burn bright among the stones, and their sweet coconut smell hangs in the air. The grass is long and soft with dew. Trails lead north toward higher ground, west over a rise, and south down the slope.
rooms.105778: From this height the land lies open in every direction, ridge after ridge of brown hills fading into blue. A flat-topped boulder makes a natural seat and is worn smooth by shepherds. The wind is stronger here and carries the cry of curlews. North the ground climbs on, south it drops, and a faint trail wanders west.
rooms.105780: The hill ends in a bluff of crumbling earth and exposed roots, where the foothills seem to lean against the sky. A scatter of fallen stones marks where some old beacon or watchpost once stood. Dry thyme crushes under your boots and perfumes the wind. The bluff slopes south, and a track leads west along its edge.
rooms.105779: A small stream, dry in summer and now a mere thread of silver, winds through this hollow between two knolls. Willow scrub grows along its stony bed, rattling its last yellow leaves. The footing is soft and the grass is trampled by hoofs, though the tracks are old. The hollow opens east to a bluff, south over the slope, and west toward lower ground.
rooms.105777: Heather and gorse cover the slope in a tangle of purple and yellow, thick enough to snag at your cloak. A scrap of faded cloth, caught on the thorns, flutters like a tiny flag. Small birds scatter from the bushes at your approach. The hillside tilts south, and the ground opens out north and east.
rooms.105775: Wheel ruts run through the turf here, the broad marks of carts that once came and went from the buildings along the side path. The grass at the verge is trampled flat, and a few dry stalks of old hay lie scattered on the ground. A rough path leads west toward a barn and stable, while the slopes go on north, south and east.
rooms.105769: A pair of ancient standing stones lean together at the brow of this knoll, their faces pitted by centuries of rain. Lichen paints them in patches of grey and orange. Beyond them the hills tumble away in all directions. A narrow side path leads west, and the open slopes lead north, east and south.
rooms.105765: Cart ruts and boot-prints crisscross this part of the hills, where the road's traffic has spilled out into the heather. A signpost stands at a crossing of tracks, but its arms have been snapped off and lie in the weeds. A side path leaves west through the bracken, and the slope runs on north, south and east.
rooms.105760: The foothills slope gently down to the wide road here, and the dark top of the castle's outer wall peeps above the grass. Fox droppings and a few scattered bones tell of hunting in the night. A side path leads west into the bracken, and the road lies south. Grey mist gathers in every dip as the light fades.
rooms.105761: Nettles and dock have colonised the verge where the hill meets the wide road, and the ground is churned by wheels. A broken cartwheel lies half buried in the weeds, its spokes rotted to splinters. The road runs close by to the south, while the slopes stretch away north, east and west. A blackened fire-ring shows where travellers once camped.
rooms.105781: The wide road is paved here with flat grey slabs, cracked and furred with moss, the work of a more prosperous age. Deep ruts run between the verges, filled with last night's rain. A hillside rises to the north, and to the south the ground falls to a bowl of tussocky grass. The road runs on east and west, and a lone crow watches from a fence post.
rooms.105701: A stub of milestone, capped with yellow lichen, is all that remains of the markers that once lined this stretch of road. The surface is hard-packed gravel with a crown in the middle, drained by ditches choked with dead leaves. The grass on both sides is trampled by recent travellers. The road continues east toward its end and west toward the castle, with paths off north and south.
rooms.105750: A low stone cairn, built by travellers and added to over the years, stands beside the path in this sheltered fold of the hills. Wild thyme and yarrow grow among the stones. The road is close at hand to the north, and the ground rolls on east, west and south. Somewhere a cowbell clanks, faint and hollow.
rooms.105751: The foothills here are bare and windswept, with a thin carpet of grass over pale stone and a few stunted rowan trees. Old wagon tracks cut across the slope from the road to the north. The land drops away to the west, where a stream bed glints in the hollow. Wind sings thinly in the rock.
rooms.105758: The ground is soft and springy underfoot, thick with moss around a seep that wets the hillside. Tall rushes grow in a ragged line where the water gathers, and dragonflies hover over the damp. Slopes climb north toward the road and fall away west. The air feels heavier here, as before a storm.
rooms.105755: A broad, bare hump of hill gives a clear view of Castle Varok's turrets, dark against the clouds. The turf is scuffed by hooves and sprinkled with the droppings of deer. Paths run off in every direction across the crest, north toward the road and south down a long slope. A stiff breeze plucks at your clothes.
rooms.105749: A rotting wooden gate stands in the grass here, its fence long gone, as if some farmer meant to shut out the whole hillside. Burdock and teasel have grown tall around its posts. The road is a short step north, and the ground falls on south, west and east. A fine drizzle beads in your hair.
rooms.105748: Short, wiry grass covers this slope, which leads up toward the grim walls of the castle. A line of old fence posts, grey and leaning, marches along the hill toward the stonework. The wide road lies north, and the wall can be reached by a short walk west. Crows wheel and shout around the battlements.
rooms.105782: The wide road curves here toward a great gatehouse, and the castle's outer wall rises in dark blocks beside the verge. Ivy has strangled one corner tower, and its leaves rustle like whispers. Iron lanterns hang on poles along the roadside, long dark. The entrance to Castle Varok lies just west, and paths lead north and south over the turf.
rooms.105702: The entrance of Castle Varok is a vaulted gate in a curtain wall of black stone, its portcullis rusted up and left forever half raised. Stone faces with chipped features glare down from the lintel, weeping rainwater. A pair of tall oak doors stand open west into a foyer lit by candles that never seem to flicker. Paths follow the wall north and south, and the road runs back east.
rooms.105759: A narrow path of trodden earth runs beside the castle's outer wall, hemmed in by bramble and mallow. The wall rises in rough courses of black stone, topped with broken battlements. The path leads north toward a farm and south to the castle entrance, and a gap in the brambles opens east onto the hills.
rooms.105764: The side path dips between banks of nettles and wild garlic, which scent the air with a green pungency. Overhead a hawthorn hedge makes a loose roof, hung with red berries. Ruts of a hay-cart show in the soft earth. The path goes on north and south, and a gap leads east over the grass.
rooms.105770: A rickety wooden gate, hanging from a single hinge, marks the beginning of the farmland that once served the castle. Thin furrows of an overgrown field run beside the path, where weeds have swallowed the old crops. A rusting plough rests in the grass. The path runs north toward the buildings and south back toward the castle, and a trail leaves east over the knolls.
rooms.105771: The path ends at a yard of beaten earth between a long, low barn and a sagging stable. A stone trough, green with scum, stands by the barn door. Ruts and old straw show that animals were once kept here. The barn lies to the north and the stable to the west, with the path leading back south and a trail east over the hills.
rooms.105772: The barn smells of mouldering hay and mice. Great cobwebbed beams hold up a roof pierced by holes where daylight falls in grey bars. A wagon with a broken axle rests against the wall, and loose straw covers the floor in drifts. The big door opens south onto the yard.
rooms.105774: Wooden stalls line the walls of the stable, their half-doors splintered and their iron rings rusted. The straw is old and dark, and a leather halter hangs from a peg, cracked by time. The smell of horse is only a ghost in the air. The only way out is the open doorway east.
rooms.105747: The castle's curtain wall towers beside the path, forty feet of black stone streaked with water-stains and crowned with leaning battlements. Narrow arrow slits, unlit, gaze out like empty eyes. The turf at its foot is bare and trodden into a path. The gate lies north, the wall runs on south, and the hills slope up to the east.
rooms.105752: Water has stained the wall in long black streaks beneath each slit, and a drain-spout carved as a snarling beast spits nothing now. Moss covers the base and tiny ferns sprout from the mortar. The path follows the wall north and south, while a way leads east across the hill. The ground underfoot is wet and strewn with fallen mortar.
rooms.105754: Grass grows thick and tangled between the wall's foot and the open hillside here, and a hawthorn thicket crowds near a place where the stones have slumped. A thrush sings from the thorn, bold in the dull light. Slopes lead north, south and east, and a path runs west to the foot of the castle wall.
rooms.105756: The hillside is strewn with a litter of old building stone, where part of the castle's outer works was tumbled down by weather and time. Burrow holes riddle the bank, and the earth around them is scattered with grey fur. The ground leads north and east, and the castle wall stands close by to the west.
rooms.105757: The last rise of the foothills on this side ends in a hollow of thistle and bramble, where the paths peter out. A fallen elm lies across the hollow, its bark peeled and bleached. The slope climbs north to open hills, and a trail leads west toward the foot of the castle wall.
rooms.105753: The wall makes a blunt, battered corner here, a great angled buttress of stone where the foundations are cracked and sagging. Lichen in orange coins covers the buttress, and high above a lone window slit stares down. The path runs north along the foot of the wall, and a trail leads east into the hills.
rooms.105703: The foyer is a tall square hall floored with black and white marble, its tiles dull under a veil of dust. A grand chandelier hangs overhead, every candle burning with a cold, still flame. Dust sheets cover the furniture, draped over shapes like slumped mourners. Doors lead north and south into hallways, the castle's gate lies back east, and an open archway leads west into the main hall.
rooms.105704: The hallway is narrow and panelled in dark walnut, its surface furred with dust. Portraits in gilt frames line the walls, their faces gone grey and indistinct. A runner of blue carpet is worn through in the middle. The hallway runs north deeper into the castle and south back to the foyer.
rooms.105705: At this end of the hallway a tall pair of double doors, carved with flowering vines, leads to the lord's state room. A table holds a dead vase of dry flowers, their petals fallen in a ring. The air is chill and smells of old roses. The doors stand north, and the hallway returns south.

105706.description: The state room is a long chamber with a vaulted ceiling, where a great table of black wood stands under a sheet of dust. High-backed chairs, each carved with a bat-winged crest, line the table, and a tapestry of a hunt on the wall has faded to brown. Tall windows have been boarded from within. The door south leads to the hallway, and a smaller door west leads to the back hall.

rooms.105714: The back hall is a plain servants' passage, whitewashed and bare, though the whitewash is flaking in great patches. Iron hooks line the walls, once for lamps. The flagstones are worn into hollows by generations of hurrying feet. It runs east toward the state room and west to further passage.
rooms.105715: A long, draughty stretch of the back hall, where cobwebs trail across the passage like torn lace. A bucket with a rotted bottom lies on its side, and a mop has stiffened into a grey claw. The silence is complete except for a drip somewhere. The hall goes on east and west.
rooms.105716: The back hall bends here toward a small door at its far end, and the walls close in. A rack of broken lanterns and a heap of dust-covered sacking fill one corner. The floor is gritty with soot. The hall leads east back toward the state room, and north to the back exit.
rooms.105717: A small oak door, bound in iron and fastened with rusted bolts, leads out to a neglected kitchen garden behind the castle. Light leaks through its cracks in thin lines, and a cold draught whistles at the keyhole. A broom and a rotted barrel stand by the wall. The only way back lies south down the hall.
rooms.105707: This hallway is hung with rich but faded tapestries of vineyards and moonlit orchards. A narrow table holds a tarnished silver candelabrum whose candles have burned to nubs. The carpet muffles each step, and the walls seem to hold their breath. The hallway runs north to the foyer and south toward a closed door.
rooms.105708: Here the hallway ends before a door of black lacquered wood with silver hinges in the shape of bats. The air is perfumed with an old, cloying scent of lilies and something sweeter beneath. A mirror in a tall frame hangs on the wall, but it is covered with a black cloth. The door stands south, and the hallway runs back north.

105709.description: A vast bedchamber, hung in crimson and black, where a canopied bed big enough for a dozen sleepers rises on a dais. The curtains are drawn, and a heavy coffin of black stone stands beside the bed with its lid ajar. Candles gutter in sconces without ever burning down, and the shadows move a moment after you do. A door west leads to a hallway, and the door north returns to the corridor.

rooms.105722: A long hallway runs along the outer wall of the castle, its windows shuttered with iron and sealed with cobweb. The floor is a chess-board of dusty tile. Pale light seeps through the shutters in narrow blades. The hall leads east to the lord and lady's door and west along the shuttered wall.
rooms.105721: Suits of armour stand in niches along this hallway, each one grey and silent, their visors lowered. One has fallen and lies in a clatter of plates beneath its niche. Dust drifts in the air, stirred by your passing. The hallway goes on east and west.
rooms.105720: A worn rug of foreign pattern lies crooked on the floor, and fringes of cobweb hang from the sconces. Bare patches on the wall show where paintings have been removed. A faint tune, like a music-box, drifts from somewhere far off and then stops. The hallway runs east, and bends away west.
rooms.105723: The hallway makes a sharp turn here, and a tall window set into the angle looks out, through grimy glass, on the dull fields beyond the wall. A stone bench stands beneath it, its cushions rotted to rags. The cold is sharper at the corner. The hall leads north into the Western Hallway and back east.
rooms.105724: The hall here is lined with doors that open on empty rooms, their hinges rusted into place. A threadbare carpet runs down the middle, patterned with faded roses. The ceiling is stained by old leaks in rust-coloured maps. It runs north toward a heavy door and south to a bend.
rooms.105725: At this end the hallway meets a heavy oak door, banded with iron, and a lantern bracket on the wall holds only a pool of congealed tallow. The floor is scored with the scrapes of furniture dragged long ago. A sour smell of cold ashes hangs in the air. The door north opens on a stairwell, and the hallway runs back south.
rooms.105726: A broad stairwell climbs from here in a long curve, its banister carved with twining vines and its steps worn smooth in the middle. A pool of dim light falls from a high window, thick with floating dust. A door south leads to the hallway, an archway leads east into the main hall, and the steps rise up into darkness.
rooms.105711: This end of the great hall rises two stories to a beamed roof, where banners in black and silver hang in rotted ribbons. A long table of dark oak stands in the middle, laid with plates for a feast that never came. The air tastes of dust and cold wax. Archways lead north to the ballroom and east along the hall, and a door west leads to the stairwell.
rooms.105712: The ballroom's polished floor stretches away in a sea of chequered parquet, scuffed by the passing of many steps though no dust lies here. High mirrors in gilded frames line the walls, reflecting the pale ghosts of candle flames. Faint strains of a waltz hang in the air as if remembered. The ballroom continues east, and the main hall lies south.
rooms.105713: At this end of the ballroom a raised dais holds the stands of a vanished orchestra, with music sheets yellowing on the stands. Long velvet drapes hang over tall windows, rotted into rags. The floor is cold and gleams like dark water. The way south leads to the main hall, and the ballroom opens west.
rooms.105710: A vast hearth yawns in the wall of this hall, big enough to roast an ox, its grate cold and swept clean. Hunting trophies stare down with glass eyes: stags, boars and a great wolf's head. The flagstones ring hollow underfoot. Archways lead north to the ballroom and east to the foyer, a passage leads south to the kitchen, and the hall continues west.
rooms.105719: The castle kitchen is a soot-black vault of brick, with iron hooks overhead and a hearth wide enough to stand in. A long butcher's block, deeply scored, stands in the middle, and copper pans hang green and dull from the beams. Nothing has been cooked here for years. The kitchen opens north to the main hall and west to a storeroom, and a heavy door south leads to cold storage.
rooms.105783: Cold seeps from the stone walls of this cellar, where rows of slate shelves hold dusty jars and bottles sealed with wax. Hooks for hanging meat gleam in the roof, rusted and bare. Barrels of vinegar and brine leak into puddles along the floor. The air is dank and still. The only way out is north to the kitchen.
rooms.105718: Sacks of mouldering flour and grain have burst along the walls of this storeroom, and the floor is crusted with grey meal. Shelves of rope, candles and spare lanterns stand beneath layers of dust. Rat droppings dot the boards, and a broken crate spills tarnished cutlery. The only way out is east to the kitchen.
rooms.105732: The upper hallway is lit by a long skylight, grimed and cracked, that lets down a grey, dusty glow. A carpet of faded red runs the length of the hall, bearing a trail of footprints in the dust. Doors lead east and west into guest rooms, the hall goes on north and south, and the stairs lead down.
rooms.105731: Portraits of pale, handsome ancestors hang along the hall here, each with the same sharp chin and dark eyes, and their gaze seems to follow you. A table beneath them holds a dish of dust and a stopped clock. Doors east and west lead to guest rooms. The hall runs north and south.
rooms.105730: A tall window of coloured glass shows a saint or a sinner, its panes cracked, and throws splinters of faded colour on the floor. The carpet here is stained dark in one long streak. A door north leads to a guest room, the hall ends east at a landing, and it returns south.
rooms.105727: A guest room hung in faded green, its four-poster bed still made with a counterpane worn thin as paper. The washstand holds a cracked basin, and a smell of damp wool comes from the wardrobe. A narrow window, nailed shut, looks out over the dull fields. The only way out is the door south.
rooms.105729: The hall comes to an end at a blank panelled wall, hung with a single oval mirror whose silvering is eaten into black lace. A narrow bench stands under it, and a candle stump sits in a dish. The door east leads to a guest room, and the hall returns west.
rooms.105728: This guest room is decked in yellow silk gone brown, with a canopy over the bed that has half collapsed into a heap. A writing desk by the window holds a dried inkwell and a quill chewed down to a stub. Spiders have strung the curtains with grey webs. The door west returns to the hall.
rooms.105742: A small room with blue-painted walls, now blistered and peeling, and a narrow bed with a patchwork quilt. A dressing table stands before a mirror whose glass is blank with grime. Mouse-chewed books lie in a heap under the window. The only exit is the door west to the hall.
rooms.105743: A roomy chamber with a stone fireplace, the grate choked with cold clinker, and a leather armchair splitting at the seams. The bed hangings are dark purple and smell of mildew. A tall window is shuttered and barred. The door east leads back to the hall.
rooms.105741: A cheerless room with walls of bare plaster and a bed of black iron, its blankets folded with military neatness. A footlocker stands open and empty at its foot. Cold radiates from the stone as if the room has never been warmed. The door west opens on the hall.
rooms.105733: A narrow table in an alcove holds a bust of a stern, hook-nosed man, whose marble nose has been chipped. The carpet here is rumpled, as if something heavy was dragged along it. Faint scratches mark the door-frames, deep as claws. Doors lead east and west to guest rooms, and the hall runs north and south.
rooms.105740: A modest guest chamber with a curtained bed and a washstand, its shutters nailed fast. A moth-eaten rug covers the floor, and a mildewed trunk has been pushed against the wall. Mouldering lavender sachets scent the air faintly. A worn door at the west wall leads back to the hall.
rooms.105734: A pair of tall pier-glasses face each other across the hall, throwing endless reflections of dust and darkness down the passage. Their frames are carved with bats and grapevines. A stuffed owl in a glass dome on the sill stares out with yellow eyes. Doors lead east and west, and the hall goes north and south.
rooms.105739: A guest chamber filled with the smell of rotting rose petals, which lie in drifts across the floor and bed. The wallpaper is printed with climbing vines and stained with brown water. A cracked porcelain washbowl sits on a stand. The only way out is the door west to the hall.
rooms.105735: The hallway widens here into a small landing, with a window seat looking out over the foothills through dirty glass. A faded cushion lies on the seat, scattered with dried flies. The air is stuffy and warm. The hall runs north, a passage leads east to the end of the hall, and a door south opens into a guest room.
rooms.105736: The end of the hall is closed by a wall of dark panelling, with a half-circle table and a vase of long-dead lilies beneath a darkened portrait. The floor boards creak at every step. A door east leads to a guest room, and the hall returns west.
rooms.105737: This guest room has a heavy, old-fashioned bed under a canopy of moth-eaten brocade, and a deep window seat heaped with mouldering cushions. A round rug, woven in ancient patterns, lies curled at the edges. A faint scent of incense hangs in the dust. The only way out is the door west.
rooms.105738: A bare, tidy room with a plain wooden bed, a table and a single chair, as though someone expected company but never quite prepared the place. The walls are hung with samplers, the stitching rotted away. The air is musty. The door north is the only way out.
rooms.105746: Scorch marks climb the walls of this guest room, where a fire once raged and was put out, and the bed is a heap of blackened sticks. Smoke has stained the ceiling in a dark bloom. The window glass has crazed in the heat. The only way out is the door east to the hall.
rooms.105745: A guest room whose furniture has been draped with sheets, so that it resembles a gathering of silent figures in the gloom. Heavy curtains are drawn across the window, and a cold draught stirs their hems. A smell of camphor lingers. The door east is the only way out.
rooms.105744: This guest room is a tidy bedchamber with a wardrobe thrown open and a bed whose covers have been pulled aside, as if its sleeper rose hurriedly. Dust has settled over everything but a clear patch on the floor. The window is hung with grey lace. The door east leads back to the upper hall.
rooms.105773: The hill slopes down toward a faint line of road, with the King's Road crossing in the open country beyond. A track of beaten earth leads north down to the intersection, and heather grows thick on either side. The ground rises east toward a bluff. A patch of nettles marks the place where an old waymark once stood.

105769.description: The two tall stones lean toward one another like old men whispering. Faint spirals have been scratched into their faces by hands older than the castle.

105709.description: The coffin is hewn from a single block of black stone, its lid carved with a sleeping figure in a long robe. Faint scratches mar the inside of the lid.

105706.description: The tapestry shows a pale lord on a black horse chasing a stag through a night forest. The stag, on close inspection, has the face of a man.

105734.description: The two tall mirrors show the hallway in perfect detail, down to the dust. No living person who stands before them, however, finds any reflection of themselves held there for more than a moment.

creatures.long_desc: A gaunt grey wolf prowls the slope, its ribs showing and its eyes burning red.
creatures.description: The wolf's coat is patchy and dull, and its eyes glow with an unnatural red light. It trails the castle road as if called by something unseen. Its lips draw back from yellow teeth.

creatures.long_desc: A skeletal servant in the rags of livery shuffles through the hall, a dust-cloth still clutched in its fingers.
creatures.description: The skeleton still wears the tattered black and silver livery of the Varok household. Its jaw clacks as it turns its empty sockets on you. It moves with a rote precision, as if it never noticed its death.

creatures.long_desc: A waltzing ghost in a gown of mist turns slowly in the arms of an unseen partner.
creatures.description: The ghost's features blur, though a dark gown and powdered hair can be made out. It dances to music that no living ear can hear. Its cold eyes follow you as it spins.

creatures.long_desc: A pale vampire spawn crouches in the shadows, its fangs bared and its eyes hungry.
creatures.description: This gaunt creature was once a guest of the castle and now serves the Varoks in death. Its skin is white as candle-wax and its nails have grown into claws. It moves in swift, wolfish bounds.

creatures.long_desc: A stone gargoyle perches motionless above the doorway, its granite wings folded.
creatures.description: Carved from black granite, the gargoyle has bat-like wings, curved horns and a gaping, grinning mouth. When it moves, stone grinds on stone. Its eyes are two points of red light.

creatures.long_desc: Lady Seraphine Varok, a vampire in a gown of midnight silk, glides across the floor of the ballroom.
creatures.description: Lady Seraphine is tall and breathtaking, with skin like ivory and hair like a spill of ink. Her smile shows the tips of her fangs. She moves with the grace of a dancer who has had centuries to practise.

creatures.long_desc: Lord Aldric Varok, a vampire of terrible age, stands beside the canopied bed, his cold eyes on you.
creatures.description: Lord Varok is a tall, gaunt figure in a black coat trimmed with silver, his face an aristocrat's mask of cold contempt. His eyes are the red of old wine. The room seems to grow darker as he moves.

items.room_desc: A narrow black dagger shaped like a fang lies here.
items.description: Its blade is dark steel, curved like a canine tooth, and the hilt is wrapped in black silk. It is cold as the grave to the touch.

items.room_desc: A heavy silver signet ring lies here.
items.description: A silver ring bearing a bat-winged crest, worn smooth by centuries of use. It is always a little colder than the hand that wears it.

items.room_desc: A gown of midnight-blue silk lies here.
items.description: A gown cut for a lady of rank, woven from silk so dark it seems to drink the light. A few silver threads shine at the hem.
The axe-head is dull with age, but the edge still bites. The haft is carved with the crest of the Varoks.

items.room_desc: A thick grey wolf pelt lies here.
items.description: A heavy pelt of coarse grey fur, strangely cold. A furrier in Garathorm would pay well for it.
